subject: Regional custody & KMS handoff — 72h transient buffer question
messages:
From: Sophia Liu <sophia.liu@healthlytics.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@healthlytics.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Quick clarification: EU pin + transient 72h processing window

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo today — the platform looks promising. Before we proceed to contracting teams, we need one technical clarification for our compliance team: Healthlytics requires EU-only custody for customer content (model inputs + outputs) but we understand Redwood supports transient cross-region processing for operational reasons.

Specifically, can you confirm: 
- Whether a temporary 72-hour buffer (for cache warm-up / burst failover) would result in any customer data leaving EU borders at rest or being accessible to non-EU KMS keys?
- If such a transient window is used, can we require that KMS keys remain bound to the EU region (i.e., keys never leave the EU and all logs referencing key material are retained in-region)?
- What telemetry/audit evidence will you provide if we require the 72-hour window be restricted to live memory/KV-only and not persisted to disk outside the EU?

Attached the DPA addendum request form our legal team usually starts from. Appreciate a concise set of commitments we can hand to procurement.

Best,
Sophia
Sophia Liu
Data Protection Officer, Healthlytics

Attachment: Healthlytics_DPA_Addendum_Request_20270615.pdf
From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Liu <sophia.liu@healthlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: EU pin + transient 72h processing window

Hi Sophia — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the addendum form. Short answers up front, then details:

- Will data leave EU at rest for the 72-hour buffer? No — our default EU pinning ensures any persisted copies (snapshots, audit exports, backups) remain in EU-only storage.
- KMS binding: yes — we can require an EU-only KMS key for Healthlytics so key material never leaves the region.
- Telemetry/audit evidence: we can provide per-request routing logs, KMS key usage logs (redacted where needed), and a transient-processing attestation that shows cache eviction timelines.

Longer detail below and a few follow-ups for ops/legal.

Technical notes:
- Transient buffer behavior: the platform occasionally keeps short-lived KV cache entries on edge nodes for read latency. These caches are in-memory; if we need to fall back to disk for pressure, we write to encrypted ephemeral volumes that are region-tagged. For an EU-pin with the constraint you propose, we can enforce a policy that prevents any fallback-to-disk outside the eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 regions.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and can require an EU CMK through our KMS integration. We will ensure signing and decryption usages occur within EU-hosted HSMs.
- Evidence: routing logs (JSON per-request) + KMS audit events + a short ops runbook describing eviction and persistence behavior. We usually provide a 30-day sample telemetry export for new enterprise customers during onboarding.

Next asks for us to produce the DPA addendum draft: can you confirm your procurement contact and whether Healthlytics requires vendor subprocessor-level attestations (we can provide the recent roster CSV).

I'll loop in Kimberly for the legal wording and Marissa for delivery timeline.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Looping in ops/legal — marking this High priority for onboarding. Notes:
- Customer explicitly wants KMS key residency guarantee and no persisted copies outside EU for the 72h window.
- Attachments: they gave a DPA addendum template. I'll draft a short addendum that: (a) affirms EU-only persisted custody, (b) binds fallback volumes to EU, (c) states KMS CMK residency and HSM use, (d) includes evidence package items and timing.

Questions for Kimberly/legal:
- Do we need to add specific SLA language around the 72-hour buffer (e.g., maximum aggregate days/year where transience allowed)?
- For HVAs, procurement sometimes wants a clause limiting transient cross-border to <72h per incident and a notification window. Do we want to concede notification windows?

Jonas — can you estimate ETA for the telemetry sample export and whether we need any ops change to lock fallback volumes to EU-only?

Thanks,
Marissa
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, chloe_martin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick clarification: EU pin + transient 72h processing window

Thanks Marissa — drafting guidance. My thinking:
- Legal will agree to an addendum that states: persisted customer data will not be written to storage outside the EU; any ephemeral/transient caching that could briefly touch non-EU infrastructure must be limited to memory-only and be auditable. We should avoid a hard absolute "never" for in-memory routing policies because of extreme DR contingencies, but we can provide a contractual commitment to notify within 48 hours and remediate within 72h if an emergency transient cross-hop occurs.
- Suggestion: Offer two tiers in the addendum:
  1) Standard EU Pin: EU-only persisted custody + EU CMK; allowed transient in-memory processing but no persisted writes outside EU; 48h incident notification.
  2) Locked EU Custody (stricter): enforce region-proof controls via our private deployment (Redwood Private) — no cross-hop allowed except manual approved exceptions; longer lead time and higher cost.

Marissa: please prepare both texts; we'll pick one based on Healthlytics' risk tolerance.

Kimberly
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Hi all and Sophia — ops confirmation below for the addendum draft:

- Telemetry: we can produce per-request routing logs and KMS key-usage events for a rolling 90-day window. Sample export available within 3 business days; full onboarding export takes up to 2 weeks depending on retention slicing.
- Fallback volumes: currently, fallback-to-disk is gated by a region policy; enabling strict EU-only fallback requires a small runtime config change for the customer's tenancy. We can make that change during onboarding; no code changes required.
- Eviction semantics: we maintain an LRU in-memory cache. In stress scenarios we may write to ephemeral SSDs; for EU-pin customers we'll configure those ephemeral volumes to be provisioned only in EU zones. We'll also add an eviction TTL (default 24h) and can set to 0 (memory-only) if they require.

Action items:
- Marissa: please send the two-tier addendum draft to Sophia and cc contracts@healthlytics.com.
- Chloe/Kimberly: please review the legal wording for notification windows and the incident remediation commitment.
- Ops: I'll prepare the 72h eviction/TTL config and the sample telemetry export. ETA: telemetry sample in 3 business days; config switches in onboarding within 48 hours of signed addendum.

Sophia — happy to hop on a quick call if you want run through the technical evidence package.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
